ru.understandingChildBirth: Understanding Childbirth: What Happens, Challenges, and Professional Help
ru.aClearSafeOverview: A clear, safe overview of childbirth — written in simple, calm language.
ru.introText: This article explains childbirth in an informative, non-graphic way. It is suitable for basic health knowledge and understanding how professionals support the process.

whatIsChildbirth.title: What is childbirth?
whatIsChildbirth.description: Childbirth is the process of delivering a baby. It usually happens in three stages:
items: Early and active labor — contractions help the cervix open.
Birth — the baby moves through the birth canal.
Placenta delivery — the process completes after the baby is born.

commonChallenges.title: Common challenges
commonChallenges.description: Some difficulties may occur during childbirth, such as:
items: Long labor — sometimes progress is slower than expected.
Pain or exhaustion — birth is physically intense, so support is important.
Baby’s position — not all positions make birth easier and may require assistance.
Unexpected changes — such as shifts in heart rate or contraction patterns.
commonChallenges.note: These challenges are common, and trained professionals monitor them to keep both the parent and baby safe.

whoHelps.title: Professionals who help
items: Obstetricians (OB-GYNs) — doctors specialized in pregnancy and birth.
Midwives — trained professionals who support many types of deliveries.
Nurses — assist with monitoring and care during labor.
Doulas — provide emotional and practical (non-medical) support.

whenToSeekHelp.title: When to seek professional help
whenToSeekHelp.description: Professional support is always recommended, especially if:
items: Labor slows down or stops progressing.
There is intense or unusual pain.
The baby shows signs of stress (monitored by medical staff).
Symptoms such as fever or unusual bleeding appear.

whyItMatters.title: Why understanding childbirth matters
items: Builds essential basic health knowledge.
Helps you support friends or family who may be expecting.
Acknowledges the physical and emotional effort involved in birth.

howItWorks.title: How It Works
howItWorks.description: Every family is unique. My role as a doula is to offer continuous, compassionate support before, during, and after birth — honoring your preferences and values.

steps.title: Initial Consultation
steps.text: We begin with a relaxed meeting to get to know each other. We talk about your pregnancy, birth hopes, past experiences, and any questions or concerns you may have. This is a space for listening, trust, and connection.

steps.title: Prenatal Support
steps.text: During pregnancy, we meet to prepare emotionally and practically. We explore birth preferences, comfort techniques, breathing, partner support, and ways to feel informed and confident as you approach your birth.

steps.title: Birth Support
steps.text: I offer continuous presence during labor, providing emotional reassurance, physical comfort, and calm guidance. I support you and your partner while respecting your birth team and medical providers.

steps.title: Immediate Postpartum Care
steps.text: After birth, I remain present to help you settle in, offering gentle support with bonding, feeding, and emotional processing of your birth experience.

steps.title: Postpartum Follow-Up
steps.text: We reconnect after birth to reflect, answer questions, and support your transition into parenthood. This time focuses on reassurance, rest, and emotional care.

steps.title: Ongoing Respect & Care
steps.text: My approach is non-judgmental and inclusive. I support all birth paths and honor your choices. You are always at the center of your own experience.
